correctness.rationale: In a vertex-avoiding central plane every crossed dodecahedron edge contributes one section vertex, so the count is constant on each strict vertex-sign chamber. Independently I used twice the stated vertex coordinates in Z[sqrt(5)], checked the 120 triple determinants, and identified all 30 edges by the largest dot product between distinct vertices. Such a nearest pair is exposed by the sum of its two vertex vectors. For each of the 90 oriented intersection rays of pairs of circles, the other eight signs are fixed and each of the four signs of the active pair is locally realized. This produces all chambers because the sign regions are convex spherical polygons and ten great circles in general position have exactly 92 regions. Counting crossed edges and incident-angle cosines recovers exactly 20 hexagons with 6 section sides, 60 triangles with 8, and 12 pentagons with 10, with the stated angle multisets. Equal angle multisets alone would not prove congruence. A separate exact Gram-matrix check enumerates the 120 orthogonal vertex-set symmetries by the possible images of a basis of three vertices; each class of sign vectors is one orbit, proving congruence. The sum of angles minus (number of corners minus two) times pi gives each cell area; multiplying by orbit sizes and dividing by 4 pi gives all three formulas and the stated decimals. The excluded great circles are Haar-null.
residual_risks: The frozen certificate records equal angles but does not directly test congruence; the independent symmetry-orbit check supplies that implication.
The conclusion is for central planes with Haar normal, not translated planes or exceptional normals.

value.rationale: The exact law is a natural, useful geometric invariant, but this finding recomputes an already available exact law and chamber census. The reproducible certificate corroborates those facts and does not supply a distinct invariant, a materially improved general method, or an independent new conclusion claimed by the record.
residual_risks: This is a judgment about the claimed contribution of the frozen record, not about the intrinsic usefulness of the law.
